doc.title: Marty Morell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Evans's health problems
summary: Evans seemed in control and professional; trouble was visible only before methadone.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Was it hard to watch, he had health problems through those years, right?
Was it hard to watch that?

Well through those years you would never know it. Bill was always very cool and always seemed in control of everything. He was a gentleman, he was very – took care of business, you know. I think it was later on actually, it got a little bit, or maybe — I would have never known. I knew through the other cats that told me. It wasn’t really that obvious. But I guess just before he got on the methadone program you could see that he was a little bit – it was becoming an even bigger problem.
Did it affect his playing at that point, that you knew?

Not really. Not really. And I think if he was feeling sick it might have affected his playing a little bit you know. But he always took care of business. He was very professional that way. He always, you know, honored any contract or any engagement and he would always make sure that he took care of what needed to be taken care of.
